clue.text: Part of lab of fine researcher

indicators.note: only a portion of the following words is wanted, so the answer sits inside them

parts.note: run across the end of lab, all of of and the start of fine

explanation.surface: A section of a fine laboratory devoted to one scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: Boffin is informal British slang for a scientist or technical expert, someone engaged in research.

clue.text: Carry sort of bale, within limits of what one can take

definitions.text: within limits of what one can take

parts.note: to carry is to bear

indicators.note: a sort of something is a variant of it, so its letters take another form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Lifting a kind of hay bale, provided it is not too heavy to manage.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bearable is tolerable, able to be endured without exceeding one's capacity.

clue.text: Engagement ring's taken inside in raid

indicators.note: taken inside means placed within the other word

parts.note: a fray is a fight or engagement
a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: An engagement ring being stolen from indoors during a robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: Engagement ring reads as a betrothal ring, but engagement is a battle and ring is just the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A foray is a sudden military attack or raid into enemy territory.

clue.text: Reluctance to move in time is holding it up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: holding means the time word wraps around the other piece

parts.note: an era is a period of time
it, reading upwards

explanation.surface: Someone's unwillingness to get going is delaying things.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is the tendency to stay at rest, a disinclination to act or change.

clue.text: Detective with large or small amount of food

parts.note: Inspector Morse, the Oxford detective of novels and television
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A detective served either a big helping or a tiny one.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspector Morse is the Oxford detective from Colin Dexter's novels and the long-running ITV series.
explanation.definitionFit: A morsel is a mouthful or small piece of something edible.

clue.text: Relating to sight seen in abandoned coalpit

indicators.note: abandoned can mean wild and unrestrained, so the letters run riot

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something visual spotted in a disused coal mine.
explanation.definitionFit: Optical is the adjective for vision and the eyes.

clue.text: Notice threat to king in random inspection

parts.note: to notice is to spot
in chess, check is a direct threat to the king

explanation.surface: Spotting a danger to the monarch during an unannounced security sweep.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot check is an unscheduled examination of a sample chosen at random.

clue.text: Record officer shortly turned over, resulting in deadlock

indicators.note: shortly asks for an abbreviated form of the rank word

parts.note: a log is a written record

indicators.note: turned over means flipped so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a major, shortened to the military abbreviation

explanation.surface: An officer's record was overturned, leaving a stalemate.
explanation.definitionFit: A logjam is a blockage where nothing can move, figuratively a deadlock.

clue.text: It's hard, still, with all locks removed

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
still air with no breeze is airless

explanation.surface: Something tough and motionless once every lock has been taken off, like a secured door.
explanation.walkthrough: Locks suggests door security, but here they are locks of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Locks are tresses of hair, so something with every one gone is bald.

clue.text: Profligate type raced around new seaside plant

indicators.note: around means the racing word surrounds the next piece

parts.note: raced means sped
N is the abbreviation for new
thrift, or sea pink, grows on coastal cliffs

explanation.surface: A wasteful person hurried around a newly planted seaside flower.
explanation.walkthrough: Thrift sounds like a virtue, the opposite of the answer, but here it is the coastal plant also called sea pink.
explanation.definitionFit: A spendthrift wastes money freely, the very picture of profligacy.

clue.text: Pondered without reaching conclusion, however

indicators.note: not reaching the conclusion means the word stops before its final letter

parts.note: pondered means thought about

explanation.surface: Someone mulled things over without ever coming to a decision.
explanation.definitionFit: As a sentence adverb, though and however are synonyms marking a contrast.

clue.text: Curly and very short, in fashion

indicators.note: in places the shortened word inside the manner word

parts.note: a fashion or manner is a way
very shortened to its abbreviation

explanation.surface: A description of a fashionable hairstyle that is curly and cropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Curly hair has waves in it, so both adjectives describe hair that is not straight.

clue.text: Garment technocrat redesigned

indicators.note: something redesigned is rebuilt in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An item of clothing devised by a technical expert.
explanation.definitionFit: A trench coat is a belted military-style raincoat, a type of garment.

clue.text: Livid because of bruising, dismal, also sad

parts.note: black can mean gloomy, as in a black mood
also means and
feeling blue is feeling sad

explanation.surface: Someone furious about injuries, and miserable and down too.
explanation.walkthrough: Livid looks like it means angry, but here it has its older sense of bluish-grey, the colour of a bruise.
explanation.definitionFit: Black and blue describes skin discoloured by heavy bruising.

clue.text: Round off, I agree, in excellent style

parts.note: to cap is to complete or top off
taken as written
figures that tally agree

explanation.surface: Someone agreeing it is a splendid way to finish things.
explanation.definitionFit: Capitally is an old-fashioned adverb meaning splendidly, from capital as an exclamation of approval.

clue.text: Creative person finding outlet in wrought iron

indicators.note: in places the outlet inside the reworked metal
wrought means worked or shaped, so the metal word is beaten into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a vent is an outlet for air or gas

explanation.surface: An artistic type finds self-expression working with wrought-iron metal.
explanation.walkthrough: Wrought iron reads as one phrase, but wrought is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An inventor devises new things, so is a creative, original person.

clue.text: Some fieldwork producing monarchist spiel?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: tossing hay with a farm tool
second meaning, read whimsically: a sales pitch made on behalf of a king

explanation.surface: Farm labour that somehow results in a royalist speech.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second reading: split the answer as PITCH FOR KING, a spiel in favour of the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifting hay with a long-handled two-pronged fork is classic field labour; a pitch is a persuasive speech.

clue.text: Decisively beat in recount, with constituents reorganised

indicators.note: the parts of the word are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An election candidate wins clearly once the votes are counted again and constituencies redrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: Recount and constituents suggest an election; constituents are just the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To trounce someone is to defeat them heavily.

clue.text: Be entitled to command as soldier, having got away from king

definitions.text: Be entitled to command as soldier

parts.note: escaping by running faster is outrunning
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A soldier with authority who has fled from the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: To outrank is to hold a higher military rank than someone, and so be able to give them orders.

clue.text: Chinese philosophy that's extremely changed Maoist?

indicators.note: something greatly changed has been altered, so the letters move around

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking whether a radically altered communist doctrine is an ancient Chinese teaching.
explanation.definitionFit: Taoism is the Chinese philosophical and religious tradition founded on the teachings of Laozi.

clue.text: Funny actor is not producer of amusing pictures

indicators.note: funny can mean odd or peculiar, so the letters come out in a strange order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A comic performer insists he is not the one behind the funny drawings.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartoonist draws humorous illustrations or comic strips.

clue.text: Diminutive daughter in dock, for example

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A tiny girl standing at the dock in court, or by a ship's berth.
explanation.walkthrough: Dock suggests a harbour or the court dock, but it is the broad-leaved plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Dock is a common broad-leaved wild plant, an example of a weed.

clue.text: What is cut by combine, ultimately?

definitions.text: What is cut by combine, ultimately?

indicators.note: being cut means split open to let another letter sit inside

parts.note: taken as written, split by the next piece

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very last letter of the preceding word

parts.note: the final letter of combine

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what a combine harvester ends up cutting.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a combine harvester cuts cereal crops such as this one.
explanation.definitionFit: Combine harvesters reap grain crops, and this cereal is the archetypal one they cut.

clue.text: Player who takes bow at home after first half of foul play

indicators.note: only the opening half of the word for the stated thing is kept

parts.note: foul play is violence; its first four of eight letters are kept
being at home is being in

explanation.surface: A performer who takes a bow at home following some foul play.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking a bow sounds like a performer's curtsy, but the instrument is played with a bow.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrument can be called a player in an orchestra, and this one is sounded with a bow drawn across its strings.

clue.text: Attempt to include a garment that's absurd imitation

indicators.note: to include means the attempt wraps around what follows

parts.note: an attempt is a try
taken as written
a vest is an undergarment

explanation.surface: Trying to work a piece of clothing into a ridiculous copy of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A travesty is a grotesque or absurd parody of something.

clue.text: In dismay, he mentions disorder

indicators.note: in tells the solver the answer lies within the words that follow

parts.note: found spanning dismay, he and mentions

explanation.surface: Someone, alarmed, brings up a state of chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayhem is violent chaos, a synonym for disorder.

clue.text: Run after swimmer or ice-hockey player, say

parts.note: a skate is a flat fish, which swims
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A sprint to catch a swimmer or a hockey player.
explanation.walkthrough: Swimmer suggests a person, but it is a fish; R comes after it, as the word after says.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice-hockey players move on skates, so one is an example of a skater.
